title: 康方生物依沃西单抗胆道癌新适应症拟纳入优先审评，全球首创PD-1/VEGF双抗再拓实体瘤版图
content:
10月23日，CDE官网公示，康方生物的依沃西单抗注射液一项新适应症拟纳入优先审评，拟用于联合化疗一线治疗局部晚期或转移性胆道癌。图源：CDE官网此次申报进展与Ⅲ期临床研究HARMONi-GI1取得积极结果有关。2026年8月，康方生物宣布，该研究在预设期中分析中达到总生存期（OS）主要终点，并达到无进展生存期（PFS）和客观缓解率（ORR）的全部关键次要终点。一、胆道癌Ⅲ期研究取得阳性结果依沃西单抗是康方生物自主研发的PD-1/VEGF双特异性抗体，也是全球首创的PD-1/VEGF双特异性肿瘤免疫治疗药物。摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库显示，2024年该品种在中国首次上市。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库本次拟纳入优先审评的新适应症为依沃西单抗联合化疗一线治疗局部晚期或转移性胆道癌。在Ⅲ期临床研究AK112-309/HARMONi-GI1中，研究人员采用随机、双盲、对照、多中心设计，评估依沃西单抗联合化疗与度伐利尤单抗联合化疗一线治疗晚期胆道恶性肿瘤的疗效与安全性。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库2026年8月，康方生物宣布，经独立数据监察委员会（IDMC）评估的预设期中分析显示，HARMONi-GI1研究达到OS主要终点，结果具有统计学显著性；同时达到PFS和ORR的全部关键次要终点。康方生物在新闻稿中表示，度伐利尤单抗联合化疗是国内外指南共同推荐的一线标准治疗方案（SOC）。公司称，HARMONi-GI1是胆道癌领域首个以PD-L1单抗联合化疗为对照、取得OS显著阳性结果的Ⅲ期研究。该研究结果已入选2026年欧洲肿瘤内科学会（ESMO）大会突破性摘要（LBA8，主席论坛），康方生物将于大会首次披露具体研究数据。二、依沃西单抗持续拓展适应症目前，依沃西单抗已在中国获批三项适应症，覆盖EGFR-TKI耐药的非鳞状非小细胞肺癌（nsq-NSCLC）、PD-L1阳性非小细胞肺癌一线治疗及鳞状非小细胞肺癌一线治疗。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库除国内市场外，依沃西单抗也在推进海外商业化。2022年12月，康方生物将依沃西单抗部分海外权益授权给美国Summit Therapeutics，交易方案包括50亿美元以上的潜在付款及两位数百分比的销售提成。目前，依沃西单抗联合化疗用于第三代EGFR-TKI治疗后进展的EGFR突变非鳞状非小细胞肺癌的美国上市申请正在审评中。此次胆道癌新适应症拟纳入优先审评，意味着依沃西单抗在肺癌之外进一步拓展实体瘤治疗领域。后续研究具体数据及审评进展，值得持续关注。参考来源：[1] CDE官网[2] 摩熵医药（原药融云）数据库扩展阅读：1. 康方生物PD-1/VEGF双抗依沃西单抗注射液获批第3项NSCLC适应症，头对头击败替雷利珠2. 2026年全球双特异性抗体核心管线深度解析：依沃西单抗OS碾压PD-1，双抗ADC强势崛起3. 康方生物全球首创双特异性药依沃西单抗再拟纳入突破性治疗，聚焦三阴性乳腺癌新适应症

title: 正大天晴TQB2102刷新HER2低表达乳腺癌PFS纪录，双表位HER2 ADC实现疗效安全性双优突破
content:
10月23日，2026年欧洲肿瘤内科学会（ESMO）年会在西班牙马德里举行。中国生物制药（01177.HK）核心企业正大天晴自主研发的新一代HER2双表位抗体ADC TQB2102，其治疗HER2低表达复发或转移性乳腺癌的关键Ⅲ期研究结果入选最新突破摘要（LBA）优选口头报告，由中山大学肿瘤防治中心王树森教授现场报告。这是全球首个在HER2低表达乳腺癌中取得Ⅲ期临床成功的HER2双表位抗体ADC。研究显示，TQB2102组中位无进展生存期（mPFS）达到16.4个月，对照化疗组为5.5个月，疾病进展或死亡风险降低约71%；治疗相关间质性肺病（ILD）发生率为2.2%。此前，TQB2102治疗HER2低表达乳腺癌的适应症已获国家药监局突破性疗法认定，并于今年9月申报上市。此次Ⅲ期研究取得积极结果，有望为HER2低表达乳腺癌患者提供新的治疗选择。一、mPFS达16.4个月，乳腺癌Ⅲ期研究取得突破乳腺癌是全球最常见的女性恶性肿瘤之一。2022年，中国乳腺癌新发病例约35.7万例，死亡病例约7.5万例。其中，约45%—55%的乳腺癌呈HER2低表达状态。TQB2102的关键Ⅲ期研究APEX-Breast01（NCT06561607）是一项多中心、随机、开放、对照研究，旨在评估TQB2102对比研究者选择的化疗方案，在HER2低表达复发或转移性乳腺癌患者中的有效性和安全性。研究共纳入543例患者，其中461例为HR阳性，超过90%的患者既往接受过CDK4/6抑制剂治疗。研究结果显示，在HR阳性/HER2低表达人群中，TQB2102组mPFS达到16.4个月，化疗组为5.5个月，风险比（HR）为0.29，疾病进展或死亡风险降低约71%。在全部HER2低表达人群中，两组mPFS同样分别为16.4个月和5.5个月，HR为0.29。全人群客观缓解率（ORR）分别为68.8%和31.0%。目前，总生存期（OS）数据尚未成熟，但HR阳性及全部HER2低表达人群均呈现获益趋势。研究达到预设的主要终点和关键次要终点，为TQB2102在HER2低表达乳腺癌中的应用提供了关键Ⅲ期临床证据。二、HER2双表位设计，兼顾疗效与安全性疗效之外，安全性是TQB2102的另一重要亮点。间质性肺病（ILD）是ADC药物受到关注的特异性风险之一，本次研究中，TQB2102治疗相关ILD发生率为2.2%。疗效与安全性的平衡，源于TQB2102的差异化分子设计。作为正大天晴首款ADC药物，TQB2102主要通过三项核心技术实现设计优化。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库一是双表位靶向。抗体端采用非对称型结构设计，基于曲妥珠单抗与帕妥珠单抗的双特异性抗体，同时靶向HER2的ECD2及ECD4结构域。双表位协同作用有助于增强受体交联及内吞效率，提升抗肿瘤活性。二是可裂解连接子。采用酶裂解型连接子，在进入肿瘤细胞后释放载荷，并保留“旁观者效应”，扩大对异质性肿瘤细胞的杀伤范围。三是DAR值调控。TQB2102的药物抗体比（DAR）为5.8—6.0，并搭配拓扑异构酶I抑制剂载荷，旨在兼顾抗肿瘤活性与安全性，突破传统单表位靶向设计在低表达、异质性肿瘤治疗中的局限。在晚期乳腺癌治疗领域，HER2 ADC的应用持续发展。原文援引的相关专家观点认为，在已上市HER2 ADC以单抗型产品为主的背景下，TQB2102凭借Ⅲ期研究取得成功、上市申请进展，以及PFS、缓解率和ILD发生率等数据，有望成为新一代HER2低表达乳腺癌治疗的潜在选择。三、三项突破性疗法认定，布局多个实体瘤除HER2低表达乳腺癌外，正大天晴还在推进TQB2102的多项Ⅲ期临床研究。目前，HER2低表达乳腺癌、新辅助治疗HER2阳性乳腺癌、经治HER2阳性晚期结直肠癌三个适应症已获国家药监局突破性疗法认定。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库在本届ESMO大会上，TQB2102联合贝莫苏拜单抗及卡培他滨一线治疗HER2阳性晚期胃癌/胃食管结合部癌的Ⅱ期研究也入选口头报告。研究结果显示，三药联合方案ORR达到84.2%；其中，6mg/kg剂量组ORR为95.8%，疾病控制率（DCR）达到100%。相关结果为TQB2102在晚期胃癌一线治疗中的进一步研究提供了临床依据。四、拓展海外市场，推进全球化布局TQB2102也是中国生物制药推进创新药全球化布局的代表产品之一。今年8月，中国生物制药公告称，公司与印度药企Cipla订立独家授权与供应协议，授予其在印度、南非及其他五个新兴市场开发和商业化TQB2102的独家许可，涉及七个新兴市场。图源：摩熵投融资数据库随着HER2低表达乳腺癌关键Ⅲ期研究取得积极结果，TQB2102在乳腺癌领域的开发进程进一步推进。与此同时，其在胃癌、HER2阳性乳腺癌及结直肠癌等适应症中的布局也在持续展开。从关键Ⅲ期临床结果，到多适应症开发及海外授权，TQB2102已成为中国生物制药肿瘤创新管线的重要产品。后续临床进展及上市申请审评情况，值得持续关注。

title: Osteosarcoma: first progress in decades with an antibody–drug conjugate
content:
In ARTEMIS-011, risvutatug rezetecan reduced the risk of disease progression compared with chemotherapy in relapsed or refractory disease
Treatment options for relapsed or refractory osteosarcoma are extremely limited, with little progress made since the introduction of chemotherapy decades ago. However, promising results with the B7-H3-directed antibody–drug conjugate (ADC) risvutatug rezetecan in the phase III ARTEMIS-011 study , opens the door to a new approach for this difficult-to-treat disease ( LBA9 ).
Study findings were reported in today’s Presidential Symposium at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October), showing a median blinded independent central review (BICR)-assessed progression-free survival (PFS) – the study’s primary endpoint – of 5.5 months with risvutatug rezetecan versus 1.4 months with gemcitabine plus docetaxel (hazard ratio [HR] 0.33; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.20–0.55; p<0.0001) in 122 adolescent and adult patients with relapsed or refractory osteosarcoma.
“It is also promising that several partial responses were observed with this ADC as monotherapy , with a BICR-assessed overall response rate (ORR) of 15%,” notes Dr Nathalie Gaspar from the Gustave Roussy Cancer Campus Villejuif, France. Overall survival data are immature, but a favourable trend was observed with risvutatug rezetecan (HR 0.51; 95% CI 0.21–1.23).
Although ARTEMIS-011 brings hope in the field, Gaspar cautions that “Osteosarcomas are very complex in terms of their genetics and tumour microenvironment , and we do not currently fully understand the biology underpinning the efficacy of risvutatug rezetecan.”
Risvutatug rezetecan combines a B7-H3 target with a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload, while other ADCs with different targets and payloads are currently under development in this setting. For example, SOT106 combines a leucine-rich repeat-containing protein 15 target with a monomethyl auristatin E-based payload, and has shown promising preclinical data ( ESMO Open 2025;10(Suppl 3):104404 ), with a phase I/II trial now planned in LRRC15-positive advanced unresectable or metastatic osteosarcoma or soft tissue sarcoma ( NCT07801222 ). “Further studies will help clarify which target and which payload offer the maximal efficacy in patients with refractory or advanced disease,” she urges.
Another aspect to explore further is toxicity , which still represents an issue with ADCs. In ARTEMIS-011, the safety profile of risvutatug rezetecan was manageable, with 1 case of treatment-related interstitial lung disease reported. “However, the haematological toxicity profile of these agents can be problematic alongside the chemotherapy currently used in osteosarcoma. title: Improved survival outcomes with antibody–drug conjugates in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer after progression
content:
Results from PANKU-Lung01 and HERON-Lung01 suggest promising second-line alternatives to chemotherapy
Phase III studies conducted in China investigated the antibody–drug conjugates (ADC) izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren), a first-in-class bispecific ADC targeting EGFR and HER3, and the HER3-directed ADC ruzaltatug rezetecan (SHR-A2009) in patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC who had progressed on prior EGFR TKI therapy. Options are generally limited to platinum-based chemotherapy (PBC) when resistance to first-line EGFR TKI therapy occurs. “There is a huge need to develop more personalised and targeted treatments,” highlights Prof. Simon Ekman from the Karolinska University Hospital/Karolinska Institutet, Stockholm, Sweden. “Both studies are positive and demonstrate that a targeted approach is preferable over chemotherapy,” he says, commenting on data presented at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October).
In PANKU-Lung01 , iza-bren demonstrated a median progression-free survival (PFS) of 11.1 months compared with 5.7 months with PBC (hazard ratio [HR] 0.40; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.31–0.51; p<0.0001) in 422 patients after progression on a third-generation EGFR TKI, at a median follow-up of 14.6 months ( LBA71 ).
While overall survival (OS) data are immature, the iza-bren group showed a trend towards improved median OS versus PBC at a median follow-up of 16.6 months (HR 0.66; 95% CI, 0.47–0.91; p=0.0058). The confirmed objective response rate (ORR) was 60.2% versus 34.5%, and the median duration of response (DOR) was 10.4 months versus 5.7 months for the respective iza-bren and PBC groups. The ongoing global registrational IZABRIGHT-Lung01 trial is ongoing with iza-bren ( NCT07100080 ) to provide data from patients outside China.
The HERON-Lung01 study also reported a significant improvement in its primary endpoint: median PFS was 8.3 months with the ADC ruzaltatug rezetecan compared with 5.4 months with PBC (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.36–0.60; p<0.0001) in 498 patients after progression on a third-generation EGFR TKI, at a median follow-up of 7.7 months ( LBA72 ). Although 19.4% of patients crossed over from the PBC group post-progression, immature OS data favoured the ADC (HR 0.70; 95% CI 0.43–1.14). The ORR was 60.0% versus 34.3%, and median DOR was 8.5 months versus 4.4 months in the ADC versus PBC groups, respectively.
Regarding safety, grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 78.7% of patients with iza-bren in the PANKU-Lung01 trial (versus 62.1% with PBC) and in 40.7% of patients with ruzaltatug rezetecan in the HERON-Lung01 (versus 38.9% with PBC). “Within the limitations of making cross-study comparisons , iza-bren appeared to be associated with more toxicity than ruzaltatug rezetecan, perhaps suggesting that more caution will be needed with the bispecific approach,” remarks Ekman, although he notes the low incidence of interstitial lung disease (ILD) in both trials (grade ≥3 ILD occurred in 1 patient with each ADC). “Overall, the findings from these trials are promising but mature OS data will be needed before firm conclusions can be drawn,” he says.
Ongoing phase III trials are also being conducted in the first-line setting with iza-bren ( NCT07680790 ) and with ruzaltatug rezetecan ( NCT07183189 ). “There is a strong rationale for targeting HER3, given its abundant expression in NSCLC and increased HER3 signalling during EGFR TKI treatment ( Front Immunol. 2024:14:1332057 ), but it may be that HER3 functions well only as an entry point for ADCs after resistance has been acquired, rather than as a strong initial oncogenic driver,” Ekman surmises. “Results in the first-line setting will be highly informative and will help to define the optimal sequence in a crowded field where several new treatments are emerging.”
Predictive biomarker studies will be important for the future success of novel agents in patients with resistant EGFRm . Practice-changing results from the SAFFRON study , also presented in Madrid, highlight the value of biomarker-directed therapy after progression on osimertinib in selected patients with EGFR -mutated, MET-overexpressed or MET -amplified NSCLC. “A lack of positive OS data was observed with the HER3-targeting ADC, patritumab deruxtecan, in the HERTHENA-Lung02 in patients with resistant EGFRm advanced NSCLC after a third-generation EGFR TKI ( J Clin Oncol. 2025(Suppl 16);43:8506 ), which serve to highlight that treating all patients the same way, without any predictive biomarkers, may not be the way forward,” Ekman concludes.

title: De-escalating immunotherapy in advanced or metastatic cancer – it is not time yet
content:
Neither inferiority nor non-inferiority of reduced frequency immunotherapy could be concluded in the MOIO trial, which terminated early
Findings from the MOIO study , a phase III non-inferiority trial assessing the efficacy of reduced-frequency immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy in patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumours who responded well up to 6 months, were eagerly awaited as de-escalation is associated with fewer side effects. However, data reported at today’s Presidential Symposium at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October) are inconclusive ( LBA10 ). “Given the statistical details, the study should be considered neither inferior nor non-inferior, but there is much to be learned from the trial,” comments Prof. Jarushka Naidoo from the Beaumont RCSI Cancer Centre (Beaumont Hospital and Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland University of Medicine and Health Sciences), Dublin, Ireland.
In this study, 340 patients with locally advanced/metastatic solid tumours who had previously achieved a complete or partial response to 6 months of ICI therapy were randomised to standard ICI or reduced-frequency ICI (12 weeks administration). The trial was discontinued at the first interim analysis at the recommendation of the independent data monitoring committee after 120/498 planned progression-free survival (PFS) events, when early signals of overall survival (OS) appeared to favour standard dosing in key subgroups, although the pre-specified PFS futility boundary was not crossed.
For the primary endpoint, median PFS was 25.0 months in the standard group versus 21.9 months in the reduced group (hazard ratio [HR] 1.35; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.9–2.0; p=0.0635) in the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population of 308 patients at a median follow-up of 18.6–18.7 months. Patients receiving reduced ICI also had a higher risk of death versus the standard group (19.9% versus 10.5%; HR 2.0; 95% CI 1.1–3.9; p=0.0286), a secondary endpoint.
The ‘pragmatic’ study enrolled a broad range of ICI-eligible patients , with more than 14 different tumour types represented. Naidoo highlights some differences across tumour types that emerged from the dataset. “While early PFS and OS signals indicate patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and urothelial cancer may not benefit from reduced dosing, the data suggest this is not the case in renal cell cancer or head and neck cancer , although the study was not powered to make this inference,” she says. In addition, while reduced ICI may appear less beneficial, this conclusion cannot be made from the data as presented. “The trial design calls into question the applicability of the results to the main study hypothesis, since such a broad range of tumour types and treatment regimens were included.”
Surprisingly, no substantial difference in adverse events (AEs) was observed between the two groups: grade 3–4 treatment-related AEs occurred in 10.5% of patients in the standard group and 9.5% in the reduced group. AEs resulted in treatment discontinuation in 7.0% of patients in the standard group and 4.8% in the reduced group.
The ESMO framework for de-intensification trials ( Ann Oncol. 2022;33:702–712 ) suggests phase III non-inferiority trials are the gold standard. However, according to Naidoo, the specific threshold used to define non-inferiority needs to be closely examined, have input from clinicians, patients and regulators, and other study designs such as beat-the-threshold or biomarker-informed trials have also informed the de-intensification field. “While the study was inconclusive, evaluation of ICI de-intensification can still be pursued with a range of strategies – e.g., dose reduction, shorter duration or omission – especially using dynamic trial designs such as Multi-arm Multi-stage (MAMS) and MAMS-Response Over Continuous Intervention , which may allow the testing of multiple intervals,” she concludes. Among ongoing trials, REFINE-Lung trial is investigating whether reduced pembrolizumab dose frequency (every 9, 12, 15, 18 weeks versus every 6 weeks) is safe and effective for patients with NSCLC after 6 months of standard treatment, with primary results expected in 2027 ( NCT05085028 ).

title: Tucatinib improves intracranial progression-free survival in patients with HER2+ metastatic breast cancer
content:
The phase II BRIDGET trial met its primary endpoint providing a paradigm change for a CNS-directed treatment intensification strategy in patients with isolated intracranial progression
Isolated intracranial progression is a relatively common and clinically challenging scenario in patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (MBC). The brain-penetrant, HER2-selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor tucatinib has previously been shown to improve intracranial progression-free survival (iPFS) when added to HER2-directed treatment in this population ( J Clin Oncol. 2020;38:2610–2619 ; J Clin Oncol. 2026;44:1597–1607 ). “Our current approach has largely been local therapy followed by continuation of the same systemic regimen. Now, results from the BRIDGET trial challenge that paradigm providing evidence on whether we can preserve extracranial disease control while adding a brain-active agent to improve central nervous system outcomes,” says Dr Antonio Llombart-Cussac from the Arnau de Vilanova Hospital of Valencia, Spain, commenting on data reported at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October).
The BRIDGET trial showed that adding tucatinib to standard maintenance therapy (trastuzumab–pertuzumab or trastuzumab emtansine) can prevent further intracranial progression in patients with isolated brain metastases ( Abstract 1767RO ). The study met its primary endpoint, with median iPFS not reached with tucatinib, significantly exceeding the pre-specified historical benchmark of 5.0 months (one-sample log-rank p<0.0001). Of 47 evaluable patients with a median follow-up of 19.6 months, 59% remained free from an intracranial progression event at 18 months. Notably, 94% of patients received trastuzumab–pertuzumab as the systemic backbone.
The safety profile of tucatinib in the BRIDGET study was manageable, with 32% of patients experiencing grade 3 and no grade 4–5 treatment-related adverse events, and 6.4% discontinuing treatment due to an adverse event. Llombart-Cussac thinks that the safety signal is reassuring but adds the caveat that, “With tucatinib, we still need to remain attentive to the known relevant toxicities, particularly diarrhoea and hepatotoxicity. Also, with any treatment intensification, issues such as adherence, cumulative toxicity, access and cost will matter in real-world practice.”
Beyond providing practice-changing results , the BRIDGET trial introduces a new treatment concept for a highly selected patient population with isolated intracranial progression and stable or absent extracranial disease for whom adding tucatinib may allow preservation of an otherwise effective trastuzumab–pertuzumab backbone. “This offers an opportunity to delay the introduction of trastuzumab deruxtecan and reserve it as a highly active option for subsequent broader intracranial or extracranial progression,” explains Llombart-Cussac. Nevertheless, caution is needed when applying this approach. Since BRIDGET was a single-arm study , most patients were receiving trastuzumab and the population was enriched for patients with well-controlled extracranial disease. Concluding, he adds: “This is a very attractive strategy for a specific clinical scenario rather than a replacement for trastuzumab deruxtecan, which remains one of our most active systemic therapies for HER2-positive MBC with brain metastases.”

title: New players provide hope in imatinib-resistant GIST
content:
Therapies with broad coverage against secondary KIT resistance mutations are showing encouraging activity and predictive biomarkers of durable clinical benefit are emerging
Some studies presented at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October) report positive findings in imatinib-resistant gastrointestinal stromal tumours (GIST), suggesting that the current treatment scenario may be changing. Once a patient progresses on imatinib, the disease is characterised by multiple resistance subclones, each carrying its own secondary KIT mutation. Standard second- and third-line treatments – sunitinib and regorafenib – are active against different alterations, but no approved single agent is effective against all known GIST mutations ( Pharmaceutics. 2025;17:923 ). This is reflected in the modest progression-free survival (PFS) gains (~4–8 months) reported in clinical trials ( Lancet. 2013;381:295–302 ; J Clin Oncol. 2022;40:3918–3928 ; Nat Rev Clin Oncol. 2022;19:328–341). In addition, patients tend to be heavily pre-treated, so new therapies are required to show clinical benefit against a back-drop of prior toxicities and declining performance status.
In the phase III Peak study , a response was achieved by approximately one-third of 128 patients with advanced GIST who failed on sunitinib monotherapy and crossed over to receive a combination of bezuclastinib (an oral, selective type 1 TKI) plus sunitinib. During a previous report from the randomised phase of the study, the median PFS (mPFS) was 16.5 months with the combination versus 9.2 months with sunitinib, and respective objective response rates (ORR) were 45.6% versus 25.8% ( J Clin Oncol. 2026;44(Suppl 16):11500 ). Following progression on sunitinib and crossover to the bezuclastinib combination arm, mPFS has now been shown to be 7.4 months and the ORR was 29.7% ( Abstract 3717RO , key results in the box below).
Eighty percent of patients who entered crossover had not achieved an objective response to sunitinib monotherapy. Notably, in those with a best response of disease progression on sunitinib, 56% responded to the combination following crossover, including 2 patients who achieved a complete response. “This suggests that the benefit of the combination is not confined to a favourable subset of patients but extends to those whose disease showed no response to sunitinib,” comments Dr Palma Dileo from IRCCS Istituto Ortopedico Rizzoli, Bologna, Italy. The combination of bezuclatinib plus sunitinib targets all known primary and secondary KIT mutations of relevance in advanced GIST, and the data strongly suggest that the added mutational coverage provided by bezuclastinib is related to the improved patient outcomes observed. Safety findings were consistent with those reported with bezuclastinib plus sunitinib prior to crossover, with no new safety risks identified.
In Madrid, a further study reported encouraging outcomes with the investigational KIT inhibitor NB003 , with activity demonstrated against a broad spectrum of acquired resistance mutations in the final analysis of a first-in-human phase I study ( Abstract 3719RO , key results in the box below). In third-line patients who had previously failed imatinib and sunitinib (n=30), ORR was 46.7%, with a median duration of response of 20.4 months, and a mPFS and median overall survival (mOS) of 13.8 months and not reached, respectively. The mOS was 19.8 months in the overall population who had received between 2 and >4 prior therapies. “The data demonstrate promising antitumour activity with clinically meaningful benefit; nevertheless, the safety profile requires more thorough evaluation,” cautions Dileo. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 84% of enrolled patients (haematological events and elevated blood creatinine phosphokinase were the most commonly reported), while 32% of patients experienced serious TRAEs. In addition, 1 death due to hepatic failure was considered possibly related to treatment.
Compelling molecular data were also presented with the novel TKI velzatinib that inhibits a broad range of primary and secondary KIT  resistance mutations, which has previously demonstrated promising activity as first- and second-line treatment for advanced GIST in the phase I/Ib StrateGIST 1 study ( J Clin Oncol. 2026;44(Suppl 16):11501 ). In a circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) analysis of patients from the study who were evaluable for molecular response, mutant KIT (m KIT ) clearance (>99% decrease in ctDNA) correlated with velzatinib clinical benefit ( Abstract 3718RO , key results in the box below). Of the study timepoints analysed (baseline and weeks 2, 4, 8 and 32), week 8 m KIT ctDNA clearance most likely predicted improved patient outcomes compared with no clearance, with a doubling of mPFS (11 months versus 5.5 months; hazard ratio 0.57; p=0.0198).
According to Dileo, biomarker research has been limited in this space to date. “The data indicate a strong early biomarker signal, which may offer a means of identifying patients most likely to derive durable clinical benefit from a KIT inhibitor,” she notes. “However, it is important to understand the difference between a prognostic and actionable biomarker. While m KIT ctDNA clearance provides an indication of which patients are likely to do well, it does not yet provide guidance on how to modify treatment for a patient without ctDNA clearance at week 8.” Whether therapy should be switched immediately or be intensified with a second agent remains to be addressed.
Velzatinib continues to be investigated as a treatment for advanced GIST after progression on imatinib in the randomised, phase III StrateGIST 3 trial with sunitinib as comparator ( J Clin Oncol. 2026;44(Suppl 16):TPS11588 ). Other novel agents in clinical development include the experimental RAS pathway inhibitor KQB198 that is being tested as an upfront combination with imatinib in the phase II SynerGIST-1st Line study ( NCT07406633 ). “Refinement of the treatment sequence in advanced GIST remains an area of active investigation, in particular whether agents with broader mutation coverage, such as bezuclastinib, could be deployed in earlier lines, and whether combination regimens may be feasible in place of sequential monotherapy,” concludes Dileo.

title: Two novel bispecific antibodies in combination with chemotherapy show efficacy in neuroendocrine carcinomas
content:
Early-phase trial results for pumitamig and opamtistomig reflect a growing body of research in these difficult-to-treat tumours
Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) comprise well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumours (NETs) and poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs), which differ in biology, clinical behaviour and treatment. This heterogeneity is one reason NENs are difficult to treat : primary sites, grades, proliferation rates, somatostatin-receptor expression and molecular drivers vary, while evidence is often drawn from small, mixed cohorts. There is a clear need for more effective therapies in these settings, and multispecific antibodies are being investigated as a way to strengthen antitumour immunity ( Front Immunol. 2023;14:1291836 ). “The rationale for using bispecific antibodies is that single-agent immunotherapy has had limited activity in these immunologically ‘cold’ tumours and bispecific antibodies can engage complementary mechanisms, for instance, to activate the immune microenvironment and T cells so that the effect of immunotherapy is enhanced,” explains Dr Jaydira Del Rivero from the Center for Cancer Research, National Cancer Institute, Bethesda, MD, USA, commenting on findings from two early-phase studies of patients with aggressive NENs reported at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October).
Abstract 2393O (key results in the box below) reported an encouraging efficacy signal with second-line pumitamig, which targets PD-L1 and VEGF-A, plus FOLFIRI. Among 31 patients with NEC or grade 3 NET and Ki-67 ≥55% whose disease had progressed after platinum-based therapy, the confirmed objective response rate (ORR; co-primary endpoint) was 40.0%, disease control rate was 86.7%, median duration of response (DOR) was 5.9 months and median progression-free survival (PFS) was 5.5 months after a median follow-up of 10.0 months. Del Rivero cautions, however, that, “As a small, single-arm study, it sets the stage for randomised trials that can define how much pumitamig adds to active chemotherapy .” Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 96.8% of patients; 83.9% had grade ≥3 TRAEs, 12.9% permanently discontinued because of TRAEs and 54.8% had VEGF-related adverse events. One patient died following intracranial haemorrhage due to disease progression, reported as treatment-related. Pumitamig (BNT327/BMS986545) is designed to restore effector T-cell function by binding PD-L1 while neutralising VEGF-A within the tumour microenvironment ( ESMO Open. 2026;11(Suppl 3):106740 ).
“The toxicity profile underscores the importance of careful patient selection , particularly in patients with aggressive disease who may already be frail or heavily pre-treated,” cautions Del Rivero, adding, “However, because pumitamig was given with FOLFIRI, not every TRAE can be attributed to the bispecific antibody; randomised data and component-specific safety reporting will be important.” She also notes that the safety findings, including the substantial incidence of grade ≥3 TRAEs and VEGF-related toxicities, may warrant careful consideration of patient eligibility and close monitoring while on therapy. “It would also be interesting to test this agent in a randomised controlled study versus standard of care to see whether durable responses could be achieved, which is a key goal .”
In a second presentation at the Congress, first-line treatment with the PD-L1 and 4-1BB-targeting bispecific antibody, opamtistomig, combined with platinum–etoposide chemotherapy, was associated with a confirmed ORR of 60.0%, including three complete responses after a median follow-up of 21.2 months in 65 efficacy-evaluable patients with advanced extrapulmonary (EP-)NEC in a phase Ib/II dose-escalation study ( Abstract 2392O , key results in the box below). In the study’s full analysis set of 69 patients, median PFS was 5.7 months, median DOR was 10.2 months and responses were independent of PD-L1 expression, although longer PFS was observed in patients with PD-L1-positive tumours. There were no reported dose-limiting toxicities, although most (98.6%) patients had TRAEs, with grade ≥3 events – commonly chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression – occurring in 79.7% of patients. Severe hepatotoxicity was not reported. “With only 6 patients in the 6 mg/kg and 15 mg/kg dose cohorts, and 3 in the 10 mg/kg cohort who were PD-L1 positive, the study was not powered for biomarker comparisons, so confirming PD-L1-independent efficacy will require dedicated analyses. Similarly, the small, non-randomised dose cohorts are best viewed as hypothesis-generating with respect to any dose–response relationship,” cautions Del Rivero.
She notes that activity across PD-L1 strata could broaden eligibility compared with biomarker-selected DLL3 approaches , although the subgroup numbers are too small to establish PD-L1 independence. “In contrast to other treatment options in development for these patients, such as the delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3) bispecific T-cell engagers, where those patients with tumours expressing DLL3 are eligible for treatment, opamtistomig has the potential to have a broader application.” Del Rivero considers the numerical efficacy data promising relative to historical first-line cisplatin plus etoposide outcomes ( JAMA Oncol. 2022;8:1447–1455 ). However, cross-trial comparisons cannot isolate the contribution of opamtistomig to an active platinum–etoposide backbone, and randomised studies are needed before the regimen can change practice.
DLL3-directed T-cell engagers are the most developed antibody-based strategy beyond the two described combinations. In a phase I study, obrixtamig produced an ORR of 23% across all doses, regimens and tumour types ( J Clin Oncol. 2025;43:3021–3031 ). A later analysis of 60 patients with previously treated EP-NECs suggested biomarker enrichment: ORR was 40.0% in DLL3-high tumours versus 3.3% in DLL3-low tumours, with median DORs of 7.9 and 2.8 months, respectively ( NANETs Multidisciplinary NET Medical Symposium 2025; Abstract 33400 ). Commenting on tolerability, Del Rivero says, “Obrixtamig, given as monotherapy, has shown a lower rate of high-grade toxicity than the chemotherapy-containing pumitamig and opamtistomig regimens.” The phase III DAREON-NEC1 and phase II DAREON-5 trials are evaluating obrixtamig further. Randomised phase III data with the DLL3 engager tarlatamab in small cell lung cancer (SCLC) provide proof of principle for the target – median overall survival was 13.6 months versus 8.3 months with chemotherapy – but do not establish benefit in EP-NECs ( N Engl J Med. 2025;393:349–361 ). Gocatamig (HPN328/MK-6070), a trispecific T-cell-activating construct targeting DLL3, has also demonstrated preliminary antitumour activity in SCLC and other high-grade NECs ( Ann Oncol 2025;36(Suppl 2):S1367 ), however, it remains investigational.
Remarking on novel therapies in this setting, Del Rivero says, “Antibody–drug conjugates pursue a different strategy: rather than recruiting T cells, they deliver a cytotoxic payload to antigen-expressing tumour cells .” ADCT-701 targeting delta-like non-canonical notch ligand 1 (DLK1) and carrying a pyrrolobenzodiazepine dimer payload is currently undergoing a first-in-human phase I study ( NCT06041516 ). “The rationale is biologically plausible because DLK1 is expressed in several neuroendocrine malignancies, and forthcoming clinical efficacy data will determine its potential in NEC,” she concludes.

title: Targeted and cellular therapies open promising directions in sarcoma treatment
content:
Encouraging efficacy profiles were reported for epsametostat, cirtuvivint and lifileucel TIL therapy from small early-phase trials
Earlier this year, the voluntary market withdrawal of tazemetostat, an inhibitor of epigenetic regulatory enhancer of zeste homolog 2 (EZH2) that received U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for metastatic or locally advanced epithelioid sarcoma in 2020, represented a setback for treatment options in this rare and aggressive subtype of soft tissue sarcoma. But targeting EZH1/2 still holds promise in this setting, as phase II findings presented at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October) highlight.
The dual EZH1/2 inhibitor epsametostat showed promising antitumour activity, with an objective response rate (ORR) of 40.0% and median progression-free survival (PFS) of 13.1 months in 75 efficacy-evaluable patients with epithelioid sarcoma ( Abstract 3714O , key results in the box below). Results are consistent with previously reported phase I data in an epithelioid sarcoma cohort ( EClinicalMedicine. 2025;86:103398 ). “These results are particularly impressive considering the efficacy of standard chemotherapy: the ORR with anthracycline- and gemcitabine-based regimens is 22–27%, with median PFS of 4–6 months ( JAMA Oncol. 2018;4:e180219 ),” notes Dr Katarzyna Kozak from the Maria Skłodowska-Curie National Research Institute of Oncology, Warsaw, Poland.
Epsametostat appears to have greater efficacy than tazemetostat, which led to an ORR of 15% and a median PFS of 5.5 months in a single-arm phase II study ( Lancet Oncol. 2020;21:1423–1432 ). “However, caution is needed given the safety data and the fact that results are currently limited to patients from China ,” stresses Kozak, pointing out that tazemetostat withdrawal was due to increased risk of secondary haematological malignancies in treated patients. In this study, common treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) included anaemia (52.1%), lymphopenia (40.4%) and hypertriglyceridaemia (36.2%), with grade ≥3 TRAEs and serious TRAEs reported in 39.4% and 7.4% of patients, respectively. “Longer follow-up is now needed to determine the risk of secondary haematological malignancies with epsametostat,” she adds.
Another targeted therapy provided intriguing data at the Congress for patients with translocation-related sarcoma , despite failing to meet the study primary endpoint. Phase II study results of cirtuvivint, a first-in-class pan-CDC-like kinase (CLK) and dual-specificity tyrosine phosphorylation-regulated kinase (DYRK) inhibitor revealed best responses of partial response in 3.6% and stable disease in 64.3% of 28 efficacy-evaluable patients ( Abstract 3716O , key results in the box below). Inhibitors of CLK/DYRK can modulate alternative splicing, a process usually regulated during gene expression but which plays a key role in sarcoma development and progression ( Int J Mol Sci. 2021;22:6047 ; Sci Rep. 2021;11:14949 ). “The low number of patients in the study with sarcomas, such as Ewing’s and synovial sarcomas, seems to have limited the assessment of the treatment’s efficacy in these populations,” advises Kozak. Despite this, a 3-month PFS rate of 85% was reported in patients with solitary fibrous tumours who had failed anti-angiogenic therapy, “who otherwise have very limited treatment options,” she says, adding that further investigation of this compound in this patient group is warranted, perhaps in combination with chemotherapy. “However, the indolent nature of solitary fibrous tumours means that using 3-month PFS as an indicator of efficacy should be interpreted with caution and more data are needed from longer follow-up of ≥6 months.”
Kozak explains that several key issues exist in developing new treatment strategies for sarcoma, not least the biologically heterogeneous nature of the tumours. “A response to this has seen a trend towards developing subtype-specific and biomarker-based therapies, but given the rarity of sarcomas, there is a question of the threshold level of evidence needed to demonstrate efficacy in such small patient populations,” she says. The approval of afamitresgene autoleucel in 2024 has provided clinical validation of T-cell-based therapies in the sarcoma setting, despite the cost, scalability, stringent patient selection criteria and complexity of manufacture and administration of these treatments limiting their clinical application. In this area, some advances were also presented in Madrid for patients with undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (UPS) and de-differentiated liposarcoma (DDLS), which are aggressive, high-grade sarcomas with very limited chemotherapy-based therapies in the second-line setting. In a study of tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) therapy in UPS and DDLS, lifileucel showed feasibility and encouraging efficacy, with 10 of 12 patients who underwent TIL harvesting receiving lifileucel infusion, with overall response and disease control rates of 40% and 80%, respectively (Abstract 3725RO) . The safety profile of lifileucel was consistent with therapy in patients with melanoma ( J Clin Oncol. 2025;43:3565–3572 ), including grade 4 cytopenias and febrile neutropenia. “Although encouraging, these results are again limited by the small number of patients and the limited data on response durability,” says Kozak, adding, “Also, secondary resistance to T-cell therapies remains a major barrier to achieving long-lasting responses. These secondary resistance mechanisms are not well understood, and further translational research is needed to improve treatment durability.” The single-arm SARATOGA registrational trial evaluating lifileucel TIL therapy for second-line advanced UPS and DDLS is ongoing.
Looking to the future, Kozak says that repurposing therapies or developing tumour-agnostic targeted treatments are important strategies for rare cancers. “Comprehensive molecular profiling of refractory sarcomas allows patients with positive biomarkers to access active therapies not available to them within clinical trials,” she explains, adding, “The clinical activity of off-label trastuzumab–deruxtecan in case series of patients with desmoplastic small round cell tumours (DSRCTs) serves as a good example of this ( ESMO Open. 2025;10:104133 ; JCO Oncol Adv. 2026;3:e2500141 ).”

title: Blood Cancer Discov：三重靶向＋OX40增强＋6天快速制造！三特异性CAR T细胞疗法为复发难治B细胞血液癌症带来新希望
content:
Blood Cancer Discov：三重靶向＋OX40增强＋6天快速制造！三特异性CAR T细胞疗法为复发难治B细胞血液癌症带来新希望
来源：生物谷原创 2026-10-22 10:02
由俄亥俄州立大学综合癌症中心领导的一项I期临床试验结果显示，可能有一条途径可改善复发或治疗耐药性B细胞血液癌症患者的治疗选择。研究结果发表在Blood Cancer Discovery上。
研究人员得以在早期工作的基础上进一步推进，该早期工作利用CAR T细胞疗法增强B细胞血液癌症的治疗。所有血液癌症中约一半为B细胞血液癌症，包括淋巴瘤和某些白血病。
该试验测试了靶向3种蛋白——CD19、CD20和CD22的三特异性CAR T细胞疗法，并使用一种名为OX40的不同蛋白来增强患者的免疫反应。
“这是CAR T细胞临床试验首次使用OX-40来增强该过程并改善肿瘤杀伤，”该研究第一作者兼通讯作者Sumithira Vasu医学博士说。“我们试验的结果可能为那些B细胞血液癌症复发或治疗停止起效后选择有限的患者带来更好的治疗结局。”
团队还使用了一种更快的流程，在短短6天内完成细胞的采集、制备和回输给患者。这带来了积极结局，且患者副作用极小。
“此前有观点认为新鲜细胞回输更可取，而我们能够证明快速制造时间和新鲜细胞回输的可行性，”共同资深作者LHM项目成员Lapo Alinari医学博士、哲学博士说。“这在B细胞非霍奇金淋巴瘤中产生了有意义的临床活性且副作用极小，并在套细胞淋巴瘤、滤泡性淋巴瘤和弥漫性大B细胞淋巴瘤中实现了缓解。”
CAR T细胞疗法如何工作？
CAR T细胞疗法从患者免疫系统中取出抗癌T细胞，在实验室中修改这些细胞以增强其杀死癌细胞的能力，然后通过输注将细胞回输给患者。
该细胞疗法通常靶向在B细胞血液癌症中起重要作用的CD19蛋白。在此前的动物研究中，其他机构的科学家开发了一种同时靶向另外2种蛋白——CD20和CD22的CAR T细胞疗法，并显示出更强的有效性。
“尽管CAR T细胞疗法已经彻底改变了B细胞血液癌症患者的治疗，缓解率高，但许多患者会在CAR T细胞疗法后复发，且往往在第1年内，”Vasu说。“患者随后只剩下有限的治疗选择。”
该临床试验入组了18名中位年龄为64岁的患者，其中16人接受了OX-40蛋白增强的CAR T细胞过程治疗。所有入组患者在接受增强细胞疗法之前，此前均已接受过中位3种类型的治疗。
“虽然我们的试验显示，接受增强CAR T细胞治疗的B细胞非霍奇金淋巴瘤患者取得了令人鼓舞的结局，但仍需要在更大患者群体中进行更多研究，”资深共同作者Marcos de Lima医学博士说。（生物谷Bioon.com）

content:
近日（10月22日），NMPA官网显示，齐鲁制药申报的4类仿制药泊那替尼片获批生产。摩熵医药数据库显示，此前该品种在国内仅原研药及成都硕德药业拥有生产批文。此次齐鲁制药获批，成为国内第2家获批该品种的药企。图源：NMPA官网泊那替尼片由武田/大冢制药开发，是一款第三代BCR-ABL激酶抑制剂，可抑制BCR-ABL及其T315I突变，适用于慢性髓系白血病、急性淋巴细胞白血病等相关患者。该药曾被纳入第一批临床急需境外新药名单，原研药于2024年9月获批进入中国市场，目前尚未纳入国家医保目录。从市场表现来看，摩熵医药数据库显示泊那替尼2025年全球销售额超过1.3亿美元。

title: 派诺生物三款疟疾多阶段疫苗伦理获批，将在澳大利亚启动I期首次人体（First in Human, FIH）临床试验！
content:
派诺生物三款疟疾多阶段疫苗伦理获批，将在澳大利亚启动I期首次人体（First in Human, FIH）临床试验
来源：生物谷 2026-10-22 15:51
Bellberry 人类研究伦理委员会批准派诺生物在澳大利亚开展首次人体临床试验，评估其针对恶性疟原虫和间日疟原虫的多阶段新型U-VLP®疟疾候选疫苗。
Bellberry 人类研究伦理委员会批准派诺生物在澳大利亚开展首次人体临床试验，评估其针对恶性疟原虫和间日疟原虫的多阶段新型U-VLP®疟疾候选疫苗。
派诺生物是一家致力于开发下一代疫苗、以满足全球未满足医疗需求的生物技术公司。公司宣布，其三款多阶段新型U-VLP®疟疾候选疫苗的I期首次人体临床试验（NCT07831226）已于2026年10月19日获得Bellberry 人类研究伦理委员会批准。
其中，LYB014针对恶性疟原虫（Plasmodium falciparum）生命周期中的三个关键阶段；LYB017针对间日疟原虫（Plasmodium vivax）生命周期中的三个关键阶段；而LYB027则同时针对恶性疟原虫和间日疟原虫生命周期中的上述三个关键阶段。这些候选疫苗将联合派诺生物自研的A02佐剂进行评估。A02是一种新型脂质体佐剂，其活性成分均为合成物质。
这项随机、双盲、对照、剂量递增的临床试验将在澳大利亚墨尔本的Nucleus Network Pty Ltd.开展，旨在评估上述疫苗在健康成年志愿者中的安全性和免疫原性。首例受试者入组预计将于2026年12月完成。免疫原性分析将与设于牛津大学儿科学系（Department of Paediatrics）的Draper实验室合作开展。
这些疫苗由派诺生物开发，旨在满足对新一代疟疾疫苗的需求。其设计针对疟原虫生命周期中的三个关键阶段，并期望通过预防感染、发病和传播，为未来消除疟疾的长远目标作出贡献。
尽管全球抗疟工作已取得显著进展，疟疾仍是严峻的全球性公共卫生威胁。2024 年，全球预估疟疾病例 2.82 亿例，死亡 61 万人。绝大多数病例由恶性疟原虫（P. falciparum）和间日疟原虫（P. vivax）两种主要疟原虫引发。两类疟原虫具备复杂的生命周期：携带病原体的蚊虫叮咬人体后，孢子体随之侵入机体并迁移至肝脏完成发育（第一阶段）；随后进入血液循环、入侵红细胞大量增殖（第二阶段）；部分虫体将分化至有性生殖阶段，当蚊虫吸食感染者血液时，虫体进入蚊体内继续发育，继而传播至新宿主（第三阶段）。
目前，世界卫生组织（WHO）批准使用的RTS,S/AS01和R21/Matrix-M疟疾疫苗仅针对恶性疟原虫生命周期的第一阶段，既往在儿童群体开展的 II/III 期临床试验中，仅展现出针对临床疟疾的部分保护效力。LYB014、LYB017和LYB027的研发理念在于探索：同时针对疟原虫生命周期各阶段以及/或覆盖多个疟原虫种类，是否能够提供互补且层次化的保护作用。该科学假说将在后续临床试验中进一步评估。
牛津大学疫苗与转化医学教授Simon Draper表示："我们很高兴能与派诺生物合作，共同开展这项首次人体临床试验的免疫原性分析工作。疟疾仍是全球重大公共卫生挑战，因此有必要持续探索创新疫苗策略，以在疟原虫生命周期的多个阶段提供更广泛、更持久的保护。"
"我们的科研技术有潜力变革抗击疟疾的方式，"派诺生物首席执行官晋博士表示，"我们开发的疟疾疫苗和A02佐剂的目标不仅是预防感染，更是要创造一个更强大、更可负担的防护盾，以应对抗疟原虫复杂的生物学特性，这可能是迈向最终消除疟疾的关键一步。"

小核酸药物在过去五年迎来了管线的爆发式增长，但高速推进的另一面是同样不容忽视的失败率。全球1368个小核酸项目中，处于研发失败、停滞或拒绝上市状态的有455个，失败率约33.3%。2021年以来，259个管线进入失败或停滞状态，其中64.4%终止于药物发现或临床前阶段。更值得深思的是，一些管线在临床试验中成功实现了靶点调控——poly(GP)下降了48%，ATXN2蛋白显著降低，外显子跳跃水平优于已上市药物——却依然未能走到终点。靶点被成功调控，并不意味着疾病进程能够被改变；药效成立之后，安全窗口与产品价值仍决定研发成败。本文内容整理自摩熵咨询《小核酸药物的下一站——全球研发演进、技术迭代与研发成败洞察》报告，结合摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库对全球小核酸项目全生命周期追踪能力，系统梳理近五年研发失败管线的结构性特征与代表性案例。摩熵医药数据库覆盖药物从靶点发现到临床终止的完整信息链条，为行业研究者识别“陷阱靶点”、理解失败逻辑、优化立项决策提供了可验证的数据底座。一、近五年小核酸药物研发失败管线：终止阶段与失败原因分布作为新兴生物技术，小核酸药物的开发仍存在诸多困难。据摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库统计，在全球1368个小核酸药物项目中，处于研发失败、无后续进展、拒绝上市等失败状态的有455个，研发失败率约33.3%。1. 研发失败风险前置近五年行业研发失败的风险呈现明显前置特征，大量管线的终止集中在早期转化与临床价值验证阶段。2021年以来，共有259个研发管线进入了研发失败状态，或是进入超过5年没有任何新进展的停滞状态。从研发终止前的进度来看，有167个管线研发终止于药物发现或临床前阶段，占比达到64.4%，其次是临床II期阶段，终止管线占比15.8%，小核酸药物的研发难点高度集中在早期转化与临床价值验证环节。数据来源：摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库小核酸药物前期研究向正式立项的转化概率较低，候选药物常脱靶导致毒性是重要原因之一。从整体研究终止的原因来看，早期研究未商业化/临床前未推进是占比最大的原因，合计占比32%。根据奥尼兰姆数据，约有40%的Galnac-siRNA候选序列在临床前的大鼠独立筛选阶段中因为肝毒性而被淘汰，而这一肝毒性是siRNA与非目标RNA发生seed区脱靶配对导致的，可见对于小核酸药物，靶向递送与精准识别是药物研发前期阻碍推进的重大壁垒。图片来源：摩熵咨询《小核酸药物的下一站——全球研发演进、技术迭代与研发成败洞察》2. 临床阶段小核酸药物推进壁垒临床阶段小核酸药物最大推进壁垒在于证明其临床价值。从不同研发阶段的终止原因分布来看，药物研发前期（药物发现、临床前）的管线，最常因战略管线优先级调整、早期研究未商业化等原因终止；而进入临床阶段后，因疗效不足、未达主要终点终止的管线占比开始显著上升。即便项目成功完成立项推进到临床，小核酸药物仍容易在临床阶段暴露临床获益不足的问题，这也表明行业在立项前的调研预测工作，仍然存在较大的优化空间。二、小核酸药物研发高失败率靶点分布在近年失败的259个管线中，有83个管线未公布其具体靶点。在剩余有靶点信息的失败管线中，涉及靶点135个，整体靶点集中度较低，较少有明显的“陷阱”靶点。但其中仍有20个靶点的开发失败率超过60%，ICAM1、SCNN1A等9个靶点失败率高达100%，体现出相当高的开发难度。1. DMD：研发热情与失败率双高DMD靶点同时具有高研发热情与高失败率。作为杜氏肌营养不良症的核心靶点，近5年有32个管线针对DMD进行研发，但失败率高达62.5%，有20个管线宣告失败。其中，BioMarin、WAVE Life Sciences曾分别将管线推进至II期与III期临床，但均因疗效不达预期而终止研发。2. TLR9：跨领域开发的高难度样本TLR9靶点作为免疫通路中的关键蛋白，近五年同样拥有较高的研发热情，目标适应症横跨癌症、呼吸系统、胃肠道、炎症、神经系统、免疫调节、皮肤病、肌肉骨骼系统与血液系统等多个领域，但其失败率同样高达62.5%（8个研发管线中5个失败）。Karolinska曾将对应药物cobitollmod推进至III期临床，但因无法达成临床终点而全面终止开发。三、小核酸药物研发失败代表性案例盘点梳理上述失败管线不难发现，两类问题最为典型：其一，靶点被成功调控，并不意味着疾病进程能够被改变；其二，药效成立之后，安全窗口与产品价值仍决定研发成败。以下四个案例，正是这两类困境的缩影。场景一：靶点调控实现，不等于疾病进程得到改善1. 案例一：WVE-004（C9orf72靶点，ASO）WVE-004是Wave Life Sciences开发的一款靶向C9orf72的ASO药物，适应症为C9orf72相关肌萎缩侧索硬化（ALS）和额颞叶痴呆（FTD），最高研发阶段为Phase I/II。C9orf72基因中的六核苷酸重复扩增是ALS和FTD最常见的遗传病因之一，其异常转录产物poly(GP)被认为具有神经毒性。WVE-004的设计逻辑是通过降解含有异常扩增的C9orf72转录本，降低poly(GP)水平，从而减轻神经毒性。临床前研究中，WVE-004能够有效降低患者来源神经细胞的poly-GP，且保留正常转录本；小鼠实验中，药品展现了长期药效，成功降低脊髓与皮层的poly-GP。2022年临床试验中，实验组出现了显著的poly-GP下降，但神经损伤标记NFL及临床功能没有显著改善，公司选择继续推进实验。2023年，在更多患者入组与进行更长期试验后，NFL与临床功能依然没有出现显著改善，公司宣布终止研发。研发时间轴：2018年：临床前研究2021年：启动临床I/II期2023年：临床结束，宣布终止研发失败启示：即使靶点调控获得预期结果，其距离最终疾病获益仍然有着距离。2. 案例二：BIIB105（ION541，ATXN2靶点，ASO）BIIB105是Ionis授权Biogen开发的一款靶向ATXN2的ASO药物，同样用于ALS治疗。ATXN2编码ataxin-2蛋白，其多聚谷氨酰胺扩增与ALS风险相关，被认为通过促进TDP-43蛋白的异常聚集参与疾病进程。临床前小鼠实验中，通过遗传学手段降低ATXN2或使用ATXN2 ASO均能显著降低TDP-43聚集并延长小鼠生存时间，展现出强大的临床潜力。图片来源：摩熵咨询《小核酸药物的下一站——全球研发演进、技术迭代与研发成败洞察》2020年启动的I/II期ALSpire研究（n=99）中，BIIB105实现了脑脊液中ATXN2蛋白的统计学显著降低。然而，在6个月的安慰剂对照期内，BIIB105未能降低血浆神经丝轻链（NfL）水平——NfL是神经退行性变和神经元损伤的标志物。功能、呼吸和肌力等临床终点同样没有改善。在超过40周的开放标签扩展随访中，ATXN2的持续降低并未转化为NfL或临床功能的任何改善。2024年5月，Biogen和Ionis宣布终止BIIB105的开发。研发时间轴：2013年：Ionis授权Biogen开发2020年：启动临床I/II期2024年：宣布终止研发失败原因：靶向机制明确且在人体内展现积极信号，但未能转化为疾病获益。失败启示：与WVE-004类似，即使设计的路径在动物模型中获得了积极结果，靶点调控也达到预期，但距离最终的患者获益仍存在较大差距。小核酸药物的新靶点开发仍然有着巨大的不确定性。场景二：药效达标，安全窗口与产品价值决定研发成败3. 案例三：SRP-5051（DMD外显子51跳跃，肽偶联PMO）SRP-5051（vesleteplirsen）是Sarepta开发的一款多肽偶联PMO（PPMO）药物，通过诱导DMD基因外显子51跳跃、恢复抗肌萎缩蛋白表达来治疗杜氏肌营养不良症。与WVE-004和BIIB105不同，SRP-5051在临床试验中展现了明确的疗效信号。在II期MOMENTUM研究的Part A中，SRP-5051观察到了显著的外显子跳跃和肌营养不良蛋白表达上升，且呈现剂量依赖关系，药物在试验过程中呈现良好的可耐受性，未出现显著的安全性信号。在Part B中，公司继续推高剂量，并于2021年观察到了显著优于已上市外显子跳跃药物的跳跃水平和肌营养不良蛋白表达水平。但随之而来的是安全性问题。早在研究早期，低镁血症（血镁水平偏低）的风险就已被识别，当时被判断为“可监测、可管理”。然而在后续研究中，部分患者出现了持续性的低镁血症，且即使在停药后仍然存在，同时伴有eGFR下降（肾功能指标恶化）。2024年11月，Sarepta宣布终止SRP-5051的开发，理由是长期安全性和耐受性的考量。SRP-5051的失败提供了一个与前述神经领域案例截然不同的教训：当疗效已经成立，安全窗口便成为产品价值的唯一裁判。外显子跳跃水平和肌营养不良蛋白表达的数据是令人鼓舞的，但持续性的低镁血症和肾功能下降意味着药物的治疗窗口过窄——在能够产生疗效的剂量下，安全性风险超出了可接受的范围。这一案例的核心启示在于：对于早期出现的安全性问题，应当尽早评估其剂量依赖性和可逆性，避免在研发后期因安全性风险积累而导致全部投入付诸东流。4. 案例四：Vupanorsen（ANGPTL3靶点，GalNAc-ASO）Vupanorsen是Ionis发现、辉瑞引进的GalNAc-ASO药物，靶向ANGPTL3，适应症为血脂异常与心代谢疾病，最高研发阶段推进至IIb期临床。ANGPTL3是一个经过人类遗传学充分验证的靶点——ANGPTL3功能缺失突变携带者具有较低的LDL-C、甘油三酯水平和冠心病风险。2016年的临床I期试验中，实验组体内ANGPTL3的表达下降83%，同时带来甘油三酯最大平均下降66%、LDL-C最大平均下降35%的显著结果。进入临床IIa期试验后，主要终点再次达标，甘油三酯相较安慰剂组下降约44%，non-HDL-C下降约18%，总胆固醇下降约19%，但LDL-C对比安慰剂组没有出现显著下降，脂肪肝、糖代谢指标等也没有得到显著改善。进入IIb期试验后，在加大药物剂量后获得了更显著的ANGPTL3与甘油三酯下降结果，但non-HDL-C仅下降约22-27.7%，LDL-C仅下降8%-16%，ApoB下降约6-15%，同时加大药量后出现了部分肝脏安全性问题，最终公司宣布终止研发。 研发时间轴：2013年：药物发现2015年：启动临床I期2017年：临床IIa期（高脂血症、脂肪肝）2018年：临床I/II期2019年：辉瑞引进开发2020年：临床IIb期（高脂血症）2022年：宣布终止研发失败原因：尽管证实能够导向临床获益，但获益不足使得药物缺乏继续开发的价值。这款药物的失败留给行业的启示是，即便已经有上市药品Evinacumab证明该靶点整体成药性可行，临床结果也证明药物的作用机制能够带来部分指标改善，但如果最终的临床获益与药物最初的开发期望存在明显差距，不足以支撑药物最终走向上市。结语复盘近五年小核酸失败管线不难发现，研发风险贯穿从临床前到 II 期临床的全流程，失败诱因已经从早期单纯的递送难题，逐步转向靶点生物学验证、分子信号向临床获益转化、安全窗口评估等更深层问题。但失败不是小核酸药物故事的反面，而是它的一部分。对于药企研发人员、项目决策者而言，依托摩熵医药数据库持续对标同靶点、同递送技术、同适应症项目的临床推进节奏与终止案例，读懂靶点冷热与失败底层逻辑，才能在管线立项、临床方案设计阶段识别潜在风险，提升小核酸药物研发的成功率。相关拓展阅读：1. 小核酸药物正从罕见病与遗传病的小众应用场景，稳步拓展至肿瘤、心血管及代谢疾病等更广阔的疾病治疗版图，是当下创新药研发领域最具发展潜力的方向之一。该类药物以10—50个核苷酸组成的短链核酸分子为活性成分，能够突破传统药物“难以成药”的靶点壁垒，通过降解、沉默或抑制特定基因表达，从源头调控疾病发生机制，同时具备作用效率高、研发周期短、平台可复用等独特优势。当前小核酸药物已形成反义寡核苷酸（ASO）、小干扰 RNA（siRNA）、微小 RNA（miRNA）、适体（Aptamer）四大主流品类。依托化学修饰、GalNAc偶联、LNP包载、抗体/多肽偶联等多元化递送技术的持续迭代，其临床应用边界不断拓宽，全面覆盖肿瘤、眼科疾病、中枢神经系统疾病、遗传及罕见病、心血管及代谢性疾病五大核心领域，全球潜在市场规模约8500亿美元。凭借持续升级的技术体系与不断落地的临床价值，小核酸药物已然成为继小分子药物、抗体药物之后又一值得长期关注的新药研发热点。本文核心内容均摘编自摩熵咨询《小核酸药物的下一站——全球研发演进、技术迭代与研发成败洞察》报告。该报告依托摩熵医药数据库海量生物医药全产业链数据，从技术概览、行业沿革、市场格局、在研管线、终止研发管线等多个维度，系统梳理行业发展全貌，精准研判研发热点与潜在风险，深度挖掘赛道增长潜力。本文结合前沿技术特征与产业落地现状，系统整合并梳理了小核酸药物的技术体系、临床应用场景、主流递送技术及行业发展核心挑战。一、小核酸药物概览：技术分类与核心价值小核酸药物（small nucleic acid drugs）是由10—50个核苷酸构成的短链核酸分子，按药理载荷可分为反义寡核苷酸（ASO）、小干扰RNA（siRNA）、微小RNA（miRNA）与适体（Aptamer）药物等。作为核酸药物的一类，小核酸药物具有作用效率高、研发周期较短等特点，已成为新药研发领域的研究热点。1. 主要分类ASO（反义寡核苷酸）：结构上通常为单链的寡核苷酸；通过与靶RNA序列互补结合，实现RNA降解、剪接调控或翻译阻断的目的。siRNA（小干扰RNA）：通常为双链RNA；经RISC复合物介导，特异性降解靶RNA，实现基因沉默。miRNA（微小RNA）：miRNA类药物可通过模拟或抑制内源性miRNA，调控相关基因表达网络。Aptamer（适体药物）：化学本质常为DNA或RNA，通过特定三维空间构象与靶标结合，蛋白质是目前最常见的靶标。2. 作用机制小核酸药物的作用机制主要分为两类：（1）基因表达调控型：以ASO、siRNA和miRNA为代表，通过靶RNA识别，实现RNA降解或剪接调控，进而改变蛋白表达水平。（2）靶标直接结合型：以适体药物为代表，通过核酸链折叠形成三维构象，直接结合蛋白或细胞等靶标，阻断或调节靶点功能。3. 临床价值这种特殊的作用模式也赋予了小核酸药物显著的临床价值：它能够针对传统药物难以成药的靶点，大幅拓展疾病治疗的边界；序列设计具备天然的平台复用性，企业可以基于同一技术框架快速拓展新靶点与新适应症；在遗传病、罕见病及常见慢性病领域都展现出极高的应用潜力；部分成熟技术路线的产品还能实现数月一次的长效给药，部分前沿研究甚至在向接近一次性治疗的目标推进。4. 关键挑战目前小核酸药物行业仍处于高速发展期，技术落地与产业化仍面临多重瓶颈。首先，药物有效成分体内稳定性不足，极易被体内核酸酶降解，直接影响药效发挥；其次，组织与细胞特异性递送是行业核心技术瓶颈，严重制约药物生物利用率与靶向精准度；再次，药物应用存在脱靶效应、非特异性免疫激活及长期安全性未知等风险，临床应用安全性仍需持续验证；最后，药物生产工艺复杂，生产成本、质量控制及规模化量产的技术标准严苛，产业化门槛较高。整体来看，未来小核酸药物的行业竞争，将集中聚焦于靶点精准筛选、高效递送技术突破、用药安全性优化三大核心方向。二、小核酸药物的主要治疗领域小核酸药物横跨肿瘤、眼科疾病、中枢神经系统、遗传病及罕见病、心血管及代谢性疾病五大市场，潜在市场规模约8500亿美元，展现出广阔的应用潜力。图片来源：摩熵咨询《小核酸药物的下一站——全球研发演进、技术迭代与研发成败洞察》心血管及代谢性疾病（2400亿美元市场）：高胆固醇血症、高甘油三酯血症、高血压、血栓疾病等。遗传病及罕见病（2358亿美元市场）：血友病A/B、遗传性血管性水肿、肝性卟啉症、家族性淀粉样变多发性神经病等。中枢神经系统（334亿美元市场）：肌萎缩侧索硬化、运动神经元病等。眼科疾病（600亿美元市场）：地图状萎缩、年龄相关性黄斑变性、湿性年龄相关性黄斑变性、巨细胞病毒视网膜炎等。肿瘤（2864亿美元市场）：骨髓发育异常综合征、胰腺癌等。其他：角膜移植排斥、慢性疲劳综合征等。目前，小核酸药物已经在心血管及代谢性疾病、遗传病、罕见病等领域展现出较高的应用潜力。以肌萎缩侧索硬化（渐冻症）为例，该疾病由超氧化物歧化酶1（SOD1）基因突变引发，传统药物研发长期陷入困境，核心原因是SOD1蛋白结构高度稳定，无适配传统药物结合的作用位点，始终缺乏有效治疗手段。而小核酸药物托夫生（Tofersen）可直接靶向致病基因与RNA，从疾病根源干预病情发展，为渐冻症治疗开辟全新路径。该药物于2023年获批上市，2024年正式进入中国市场，落地惠及国内罕见病患者，充分印证了小核酸药物的独特临床价值。三、小核酸药物的主要递送方式递送技术被普遍视为小核酸药物研发的核心胜负手。当前上市产品以化学修饰及GalNAc偶联最为常见，同时以LNP（脂质纳米颗粒）及抗体/多肽偶联探索肝外靶向。1. 化学修饰直接给药主要用于ASO与适体药物，常见给药部位为玻璃体内、鞘内、皮下与局部。其核心逻辑是依靠PS／2’位修饰或PEG化增强稳定性，无需复杂载体。作为最成熟的技术路线，它特别适合局部用药或可直接到达靶组织的场景，代表药品包括Fomivirsen、Nusinersen、Tofersen（托夫生）与Pegaptanib。2. GalNAc偶联主要用于以siRNA为主、部分ASO的药物，靶向肝细胞ASGPR，可实现皮下注射、低频给药与明确的肝靶向，是当前肝靶向小核酸的核心平台。代表产品包括Givosiran、Lumasiran、Inclisiran（英克司兰钠）、Vutrisiran与Eplontersen。3. LNP包载主要用于以siRNA为主、部分miRNA及双链RNA的探索。其递送逻辑是包载保护核酸，促进细胞摄取与内体逃逸，适用于需要系统给药、需要额外包载保护的RNA载荷。其系统性递送验证充分，但产品数量少于GalNAc，代表产品为Patisiran。4. 抗体/多肽偶联主要用于ASO与siRNA，目标是突破肝外组织，聚焦肌肉、心肌及中枢神经系统；其核心价值在于利用受体介导内吞实现细胞定向递送。该路线临床推进较快，是肝外递送的重要方向，代表在研项目包括Del-desiran（AOC 1001）、DYNE-101等。需要补充的是，化学修饰是多数小核酸药物的技术基础，与LNP或偶联策略并非互斥关系——GalNAc-siRNA、LNP-siRNA通常同样采用2’位修饰及磷硫酰键等化学修饰手段。递送方式的演进也并非简单的代际替代，而是在用药便利性、靶向可及目标等方向上的持续拓展。除上述四种方式外，外泌体、无机纳米颗粒（金、氧化铁、硅等）等多种递送策略也处于探索之中。结语从首个反义药物问世，到GalNAc技术平台的成熟，再到抗体偶联递送向肝外组织进军，小核酸药物已完成从“概念验证”到“商业化兑现”的关键跨越。展望未来，靶点选择的精准化、递送系统的组织拓展化、化学修饰与安全性优化的持续迭代，将共同决定这一赛道的下一批赢家。对于身处其中的研发者与决策者而言，唯有建立在对全球研发数据持续追踪与深入洞察之上的判断，才能在技术迭代与研发成败交织的浪潮中把握先机。资料来源：1. title: NANOBIOTIX公布JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3)联合免疫检查点抑制剂治疗抗PD-1耐药黑色素瘤的I期最终数据【AI生成】
content:
临床阶段生物制药公司NANOBIOTIX在2026年欧洲肿瘤内科学会（ESMO）年会上公布了其正在进行的1100号I期研究的最终更新数据。该研究评估了JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3)联合立体定向放射治疗（SBRT）及免疫检查点抑制剂（nivolumab或pembrolizumab），作为二线及以上疗法，用于治疗经多线治疗失败且对抗PD-1疗法产生耐药的晚期原发性皮肤黑色素瘤患者。在24名重度预处理的患者中，数据显示出可接受的安全性特征及早期疗效信号：根据RECIST 1.1标准，总体缓解率（ORR）为41.7%（含4例完全缓解），疾病控制率（DCR）达75%，中位总生存期（OS）为17.8个月。探索性分析发现，IL-1β是治疗后血浆中增加最多的细胞因子，提示其与治疗诱导的抗肿瘤免疫相关。研究者认为这些初步结果值得在针对抗PD-1初治或难治性黑色素瘤患者的随机临床试验中进一步验证。

10月20日，摩熵医药中国药品审评数据库显示，康缘药业联合图锋医药、北峰药业及上海中医药大学申报的中药1.1类新药十味安肠颗粒获批临床，拟用于溃疡性结肠炎。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库一、聚焦溃疡性结肠炎，康缘再推创新中药十味安肠颗粒由江苏康缘药业股份有限公司联合上海图锋医药科技有限公司、辽宁北峰药业有限公司及上海中医药大学共同研发，是一款基于中医临床经验方开发的现代中药颗粒制剂。据摩熵医药数据库显示，该药于2026年8月12日首次提交临床试验申请，受理号为CXZL2600075，并于10月20日首次获批临床。图源：摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库此次获批的适应症为溃疡性结肠炎。作为中药1.1类创新药，十味安肠颗粒后续临床研究进展及疗效、安全性数据值得关注。康缘药业在肠道疾病领域已有其他创新中药布局。公司另一款中药1.1类新药健脾疏肝固本颗粒此前已获得临床试验默示许可，拟用于腹泻型肠易激综合征（肝郁脾虚证）。两款产品针对不同适应症，体现了公司在中药创新药领域的持续布局。在成熟中成药方面，康缘药业拥有天舒胶囊、天舒片、苁蓉总苷胶囊等独家产品，属于神经系统疾病用药领域。摩熵医药数据库显示，天舒胶囊2025年全终端销售额超过2亿元，2026年上半年销售额约0.68亿元。

content:

title: 齐鲁制药1类创新生物药QLS2401获批临床，靶向三靶点布局前列腺癌免疫治疗
content:
10月14日，摩熵医药中国药品审评数据库显示，齐鲁制药自主研发的1类创新生物药QLS2401注射液获得国家药品监督管理局药品审评中心（CDE）临床试验默示许可，拟用于治疗转移性去势抵抗性前列腺癌（mCRPC）。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库QLS2401是一款同时靶向PSMA、STEAP1和CD3的三特异性T细胞衔接器（TCE）。其通过双肿瘤抗原识别与T细胞募集相结合的设计，探索前列腺癌免疫治疗的新路径。此次获准开展临床试验，意味着QLS2401进入临床开发阶段。其双靶点设计能否在肿瘤抗原表达异质性等情况下展现优势，还有待后续临床研究验证。一、三靶点设计，探索前列腺癌免疫治疗新路径转移性去势抵抗性前列腺癌是前列腺癌治疗中的重要挑战之一，患者仍存在未被满足的治疗需求。QLS2401采用三特异性T细胞衔接器设计，同时识别肿瘤相关抗原PSMA、STEAP1，并结合T细胞表面的CD3，旨在将T细胞募集至肿瘤细胞附近，激活T细胞介导的肿瘤杀伤作用。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库与仅针对单一肿瘤抗原的策略相比，PSMA与STEAP1双靶点设计有望提高对不同抗原表达状态肿瘤细胞的识别能力，并降低单一抗原表达下降所导致的免疫逃逸风险。此外，QLS2401还通过优化CD3亲和力及肿瘤抗原结合设计，尝试在增强抗肿瘤活性的同时优化分子特性。不过，这些设计能否转化为更好的疗效和安全性，仍需临床数据进一步验证。二、临床前研究显示潜力，低抗原表达模型值得关注根据现有临床前研究数据，QLS2401在不同抗原表达水平的肿瘤模型中展现出一定的抗肿瘤活性。在PSMA或STEAP1中等、低表达的细胞模型中，QLS2401的杀伤活性优于同类对照分子。在细胞系来源异种移植（CDX）和患者来源异种移植（PDX）肿瘤模型中，该药也表现出抗肿瘤活性，尤其在低抗原表达模型中显示出相对优势。这些结果为QLS2401的双靶点设计提供了临床前依据，也使其在肿瘤抗原表达异质性方面的潜在价值受到关注。但需要指出，临床前模型的结果不能直接预测人体中的疗效。QLS2401能否在患者中实现有效的肿瘤控制，以及其安全性、耐受性和适用人群如何，仍有待临床试验回答。三、今年19款生物药获批临床，齐鲁制药持续拓展创新管线QLS2401的临床获批，也是齐鲁制药今年生物药研发进展的一部分。据相关统计，2026年以来，齐鲁制药已有25余款1类新药获批临床，其中19款为生物药1类新药。上述19款生物药中，13款为首次获批临床的新品，覆盖双靶点融合蛋白、双抗及多抗、抗体偶联药物（ADC）等多个研发方向。

title: 石药集团首款三抗SYS6088与ADC新药SYS6062同日获批临床，晚期实体瘤布局双线加速
content:
10月15日，石药集团宣布，集团开发的SYS6088注射液和SYS6062均获NMPA批准开展临床试验，拟用于晚期实体瘤。图源：企业公告其中，SYS6088是石药集团布局的首个三特异性抗体（以下简称“三抗”），靶向PD-1、VEGFA和CTLA-4。随着这一产品获批临床，石药集团正式进入三抗研发赛道。一、首个三抗获批临床，聚焦三靶点协同SYS6088是一款PD-1/VEGFA/CTLA-4三特异性抗体，本次获批临床拟单药用于晚期/转移性实体瘤。摩熵医药数据库显示，该品种在2026年9月首次申请临床，10月15日，石药集团宣布获批临床。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库从作用机制来看，该产品试图通过同时作用于三个靶点，协同调节肿瘤免疫微环境。其中，PD-1和CTLA-4均与T细胞免疫调控有关，VEGFA则参与肿瘤血管生成及肿瘤微环境调节。通过整合上述靶点，SYS6088旨在兼顾解除免疫抑制、促进T细胞活化与扩增，以及抑制肿瘤血管生成等作用。此外，该产品还对Fc端进行了改造，以降低潜在毒性风险并延长药物半衰期。据披露，临床前研究显示，SYS6088在多种恶性肿瘤模型中表现出抗肿瘤活性。至于其多靶点设计能否转化为临床疗效优势，以及安全性是否能够得到验证，仍有待后续临床研究回答。二、三抗与ADC同步推进，石药集团丰富肿瘤管线截至目前，石药集团已有70余款1类新药处于获批临床及以上阶段。除SYS6088外，石药集团另一款新药SYS6062也于同日获NMPA批准在中国开展临床试验，拟用于晚期实体瘤。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库SYS6062是一款抗体偶联药物（ADC），通过抗体识别肿瘤细胞相关靶点，将细胞毒性载荷递送至细胞内，以发挥抗肿瘤作用。临床前研究显示，该产品在多种癌症模型中表现出抗肿瘤活性。从三抗到ADC，两款新药采用了不同的抗肿瘤策略。其中，SYS6088聚焦多靶点免疫调节，SYS6062则通过抗体实现细胞毒性载荷的靶向递送。

content:
加拿大英属哥伦比亚大学Josef M. Penninger团队在《Cell Stem Cell》发表研究，针对1型糖尿病治疗中干细胞来源胰岛类器官（PIOs）因血管化不足导致移植后β细胞大量死亡的难题，提出新解决方案。研究人员利用人血管类器官（BVOs）与干细胞来源胰岛共培养，构建出带有器官特异性毛细血管网络的血管化胰岛类器官（VPIOs）。研究发现，β细胞分泌的VEGFA驱动内皮细胞获得“窗孔”结构等胰岛特异性特征，而血管细胞分泌的BMP4促进β细胞成熟并增强其抗缺氧能力。在糖尿病小鼠模型中，皮下移植VPIOs实现了长期血糖正常化，疗效与原代人胰岛相当，显著优于未血管化类器官。该研究揭示了胰岛细胞与血管的双向互作机制，为干细胞来源胰岛移植提供了新策略，但也指出需进一步解决外分泌细胞残留、临床基质替代及体外成熟度等问题。

title: Cell：免疫治疗副作用背后的“脆弱细胞”被锁定，40%患者受影响，新靶点有望让更多人坚持抗癌治疗
content:
Cell：免疫治疗副作用背后的“脆弱细胞”被锁定，40%患者受影响，新靶点有望让更多人坚持抗癌治疗
来源：生物谷原创 2026-10-26 11:24
研究团队创建了一种免疫相关不良事件的小鼠模型。通过在免疫检查点抑制剂治疗前和治疗期间给小鼠喂食一种特殊的人类样饮食，该模型复制了人类不良事件的许多免疫和微生物组特征。
在一项新的研究中，匹兹堡大学的科学家揭示了可导致高达40%的免疫治疗患者出现严重副作用的不稳定免疫细胞，并证明饮食和微生物组组成影响副作用的严重程度。这项发表在Cell上的研究发现，在小鼠中，通过关闭“脆弱”免疫细胞中的一种蛋白质，可以逆转炎症。
“免疫相关不良事件是一个巨大的问题，可能极大影响患者的生活质量。在许多情况下，它影响患者继续接受免疫治疗或从治疗中获益的能力，”资深作者、匹兹堡大学医学院免疫学系助理教授Abigail Overacre-Delgoffe博士说。
美国食品药品管理局（FDA）尚未批准针对免疫相关不良事件的治疗方法，这是免疫检查点抑制剂（一种癌症免疫疗法）的严重副作用。
接受免疫检查点抑制剂的患者中，高达25%会出现严重不良事件，导致住院并终止治疗。其变异性使得在人类中研究它们具有挑战性，而动物模型迄今未能复制人类免疫相关炎症的复杂性。
围绕饮食构建模型
“大多数现有小鼠模型依赖于基因改造小鼠或实验条件，并未真正捕捉到我们在患者中看到的变异性，”第一作者、Overacre-Delgoffe实验室博士后助理Dipyaman Patra博士说。“这让我们思考，常见的生活方式因素，特别是饮食和肠道微生物组，是否可能在免疫治疗开始之前就影响宿主免疫系统。”
Overacre-Delgoffe领导的研究团队创建了一种免疫相关不良事件的小鼠模型。通过在免疫检查点抑制剂治疗前和治疗期间给小鼠喂食一种特殊的人类样饮食，该模型复制了人类不良事件的许多免疫和微生物组特征。
“我们能够生成首个无需完全基因敲除的不良事件临床前小鼠模型，”Overacre-Delgoffe说。“通过将这种新型临床前模型与患者数据相结合，我们能够鉴定出一种全新的不良事件机制，希望这将带来新的靶向疗法，使更多癌症患者能够继续治疗并远离医院。”
免疫检查点抑制剂的工作原理是去除称为T细胞的免疫细胞上的刹车，使它们能够更好地对抗癌症。但去除T细胞上的刹车也会影响其他组织，在某些患者中导致过度活跃的免疫细胞攻击健康组织。根据免疫检查点抑制剂的类型，20%至40%的患者会经历这些不良事件，严重程度足以中断治疗。
饮食暴露调节性T细胞的脆弱性
Overacre-Delgoffe怀疑创建动物模型的答案可能在肠道中找到。她之前的工作表明，饮食和肠道微生物组可以影响癌症患者的结局和对免疫治疗的反应。
研究人员在免疫检查点抑制剂治疗开始前两周给小鼠喂食低纤维、高脂肪和高加工碳水化合物的“西式”饮食。
这些小鼠不仅在免疫治疗期间易发生不良事件，还显示出调节性T细胞脆弱的迹象，即抑制过度免疫反应的调节性T细胞因应激而变得不稳定。研究人员随后在从免疫治疗患者收集的调节性T细胞中观察到了同样的脆弱性，这些患者患有严重的免疫相关不良事件，而没有副作用的患者则没有。
恢复细胞稳定性显著降低了免疫相关不良事件的严重程度，表明调节性T细胞脆弱性是副作用的主要潜在原因。研究团队能够通过特异性阻断调节性T细胞上的一种免疫信号蛋白，以及通过将小鼠切换到高纤维饮食或给予代谢物补充，来恢复稳定性。
微生物组转移改变炎症
喂食西式饮食的小鼠还表现出与人类免疫相关炎症相似的微生物组变化。从西式饮食喂养的小鼠到常规（高纤维）饮食小鼠的粪便微生物组转移引起了肠道炎症。从雄性小鼠（对严重不良事件较不敏感）到雌性小鼠的粪便转移降低了其炎症严重程度，表明微生物组影响免疫相关不良事件的严重程度。
此外，从食用西式饮食的患者到无菌小鼠的粪便微生物组转移导致免疫相关不良事件严重程度增加，表明饮食和肠道微生物组是这些毒性副作用的原因。
可能保留治疗的靶点
新的小鼠模型将作为研究人员的平台，以研究为什么一些患者经历严重不良事件，并帮助鉴定可能预测谁最易感的标志物。
“我们现在有一些潜在的靶点正在追求，它们似乎能限制免疫相关不良事件而不负面影响免疫治疗，这将是同类首创，非常令人兴奋，”Overacre-Delgoffe说。
未来的研究将探索潜在的组织特异性药物靶点，以限制或消除副作用而不干扰免疫治疗。代谢物补充也显示出希望，作为一种干预措施，可在不干扰微生物组的情况下降低对免疫相关不良事件的易感性。（生物谷Bioon.com）
